content.comment_body: When selecting your [product_name], how do you decide between relay contacts or transistor outputs?
This choice depends entirely on your specific application.

Transistor outputs provide a fixed output voltage, usually matching the supply voltage of the [product_name], for example 24VDC. Relay contacts, on the other hand, are potential-free, meaning they aren't tied to the [product_name] power supply and can be used with various voltages as needed. For example, you could connect Q1 to 230VAC, Q2 to 24VDC, and Q3 to 12VAC, depending on your requirements. Transistor outputs offer faster switching (such as for PWM applications), operate silently, and feature internal current limiting for protection, while relays can be heard when switching.
